full_details: Morning rehearsal at the Cross Keys. The plot stayed on the door. You speak, and then you sit, and nobody rewrote the book. Between rehearsal and the play you were at the lodging with a page of Berowne. At two you read the bill for Errors and the Rose's bill for Set at Maw, and you did not cross the river. Errors in the afternoon. You played Egeon, and then you waited two hours in a cold parlour. In the tiring-room the talk was the Admiral's men: the second Tamburlaine at the Rose yesterday, and before the Queen at Greenwich by candle-time. Kemp stood on a hamper with a stool for a chariot and roared the line. The room went quiet. Heminges said they will be paid as slowly as we are. Pope said she is keeping two dogs and feeding neither. Kemp roared it again. Burbage threw a stuffed glove. The sheets of Berowne stayed under your arm. You did not read them. At home you kept the decision in one sentence.
one_sentence: You rehearsed the old man, sat two hours in the cold after you had spoken, and heard Kemp do Alleyn on a hamper until a glove ended it.
title: Sat two hours in the cold and heard Kemp on a hamper
